title: Magic Character Advancement
heading: Advancement
summary: Magic characters can gain and spend experience points like other characters, but their Might Score is subtracted from the Advancement Total; consuming vis reduces that penalty.
quotes: the character's Might Score is always subtracted from its Advancement Total
If the character consumes a pawn of magic vis of any type, he may reduce the penalty to his Advancement Total by two

title: Magic Qualities and Initiation Scripts
heading: Magic Qualities and Initiation Scripts
summary: Describes how a rare book could teach a magic being new Magic Qualities, treated like an Initiation Script adapted by a Mystagogue.

title: Transformation
heading: Transformation
summary: Experience points can be spent to gain, swap or upgrade Magic Qualities and Inferiorities according to a cost table, or vis can be consumed as a transformational study source.
quotes: Practicing a Quality that you already possess with the intention of improving upon it has a Study Total of 5
The character must use a number of pawns of vis of any type equal to its Might Score.

title: Acclimation
heading: Acclimation
summary: Each year a magic character that stays away from Magic loses a Magic Quality or a point of Might unless it meets one of three protective conditions.
quotes: a magic character either loses a Magic Quality, or else reduces its Might Score by 1

title: Acclimation: Auras
heading: Auras
summary: A table of the minimum Magic aura strength, by Might Score and time spent within it, needed to avoid Acclimation, with a rule for visiting the Magic Realm.
quotes: treat the Magic Realm as an aura of 10 and halve the character's Might Score

title: Acclimation: Effects
heading: Effects
summary: A magic character avoids Acclimation by affecting, or being affected by, a non-Might character with magic for a number of seasons each year, given by a table of Might or effect level.
quotes: a magic character with Might 15 would need to constantly affect a mundane character for three seasons every year

title: Acclimation: Vis
heading: Vis
summary: A magic character avoids Acclimation for a year by consuming a Might-based number of pawns of vis, and then rolls on the Vis Consumption chart.
quotes: A magic character is safe any year in which it consumes (Magic Might Score / 2) pawns of magic vis, of any type.

title: Vis Consumption
heading: Vis Consumption
summary: A stress-die chart for the side effects, botches, story events and Transformation that result when a magic character consumes vis to avoid Acclimation.
quotes: roll a stress die and consult the following chart. The number of botch dice is equal to the number of pawns of vis consumed.

title: Essential Traits
heading: Essential Traits
summary: Personality Traits of magic characters become fixed Essential Traits that protect against effects forcing contrary behaviour, and Characteristic-specialty traits combine with Characteristics by a set method.
quotes: if the Characteristic is positive and the Trait is beneficial, use the greater of the two; if the Characteristic is negative and the Trait is detrimental, use the lesser of the two; otherwise, add the Trait to the Characteristic

title: Suggested Familiars by Art
heading: Suggested Familiars by Art
summary: A list of animals suited to bonding as familiars for each Technique and Form.
quotes: The Arts used to bond a familiar must correspond to either the animal itself, or its powers

title: Beasts of Virtue
heading: Beasts of Virtue
summary: Introduces Beasts of Virtue, rare epitomes of their species that make good familiars, and notes the vis contained in their corpses.
quotes: The corpse of a Beast of Virtue typically contains 1 pawn of vis for each 5 points (or fraction) of Might it possessed

title: Designing Beasts of Virtue
heading: Designing Beasts of Virtue
summary: Beasts of Virtue use the Chapter 4 magical character rules with set Inherited Virtues and Flaws and no physical-defect Flaws.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Magic Animal; Essential Virtue (Major or Minor)

title: Beast of Virtue: Concept
heading: Concept
summary: Rules for Characteristics, the required Magic Animal and Essential Virtues, and permitted Virtues and Flaws when creating a Beast of Virtue.
quotes: You have 7 points to spend on Characteristics, just as other characters.

title: Beast of Virtue: Season and Abilities
heading: Season and Abilities
summary: How a Beast of Virtue's season of life sets its age and how its experience points must be spent on species Abilities.

title: Beast of Virtue: Might and Qualities
heading: Might and Qualities
summary: Guidance on spending Might on Magical Qualities, with powers restricted to those that express the species' perfection.
quotes: determine its Might and spend these points on Magical Qualities, taking Magical Inferiorities if you want more points to spend

title: Beast of Virtue: Finishing Touches
heading: Finishing Touches
summary: Natural weapons, Protection and species Qualities for animals, and the reminder to subtract Size from initial Might.
quotes: Remember to subtract the Size of a Beast of Virtue from the initial Might score to get the final Might score.

title: Birds of Nephelococcygia
heading: Birds of Nephelococcygia
summary: Describes the cloud regio of Nephelococcygia, how to enter it, and the Inherited Virtues and Flaws of the intelligent birds who live there.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Homing Instinct, Keen Vision, Lightning Reflexes.
an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9

title: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia
heading: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia
summary: The set of Greater Powers available to Birds of Nephelococcygia, each given with its Hermetic guideline breakdown.

title: Bird Flight
heading: Flight
summary: Flight is natural to these birds and needs no roll under normal conditions; difficult conditions call for a flying roll.
quotes: he has an initiative of Qik + Athletics (flying) for this maneuver
a roll (Dexterity + Athletics(flying) + stress die) may be required to take to the air

title: The Magical Lineages of Cats
heading: The Magical Lineages of Cats
summary: Introduces the three cat lineages descended from familiars of the Founders, whose magical features breed almost true.

title: Cat Character Template
heading: Cat Character Template
summary: A worked template showing how to build a magical cat character from the mundane stats and magical additions.
quotes: Cats may only have 10 points of Qualities
Might divided by 5, rounded up

title: Cats as Example
heading: Cats as Example
summary: Explains that the cat section is a model for building power lists for other species, borrowing powers and following the same guidelines.

title: Black Lineage of Cats
heading: Black Lineage
summary: Describes the Black Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

title: White Lineage of Cats
heading: White Lineage
summary: Describes the White Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

title: Tortoiseshell Lineage of Cats
heading: Tortoiseshell Lineage
summary: Describes the Tortoiseshell Lineage, its rare males, and its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

title: Cat Magical Powers
heading: Magical Powers
summary: Each purchase of a Greater or Lesser Magical Power Quality gives a cat one power chosen from the lists.
quotes: Players designing cats select one magical power for each purchase of the Greater Magical Power or Lesser Magical Power Qualities.

title: Cats' Greater and Lesser Powers
heading: Cats' Greater or Lesser Magical Powers
summary: Rules for the spell-level cost, Penetration Score, Might cost and Initiative Bonus of cat powers.
quotes: A Penetration Score = Might of the cat (5 x the cost of the power) + the cat's Penetration Bonus.
The Initiative Bonus for a Lesser Power is equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude x 2).

title: Warder's Walk
heading: Warder's Walk
summary: A cat power letting several cats combine their other powers in a ritual to penetrate Magic Resistance, at the risk of a fatal botch as more cats join.
quotes: It is a variant of *Wizard's Communion*.

title: Black Cat Wards
heading: Black Cat Wards
summary: Describes the ward powers Black Lineage cats use, singly or in procession, to protect a home or settlement against minor faeries and demons.

title: Personal Magical Powers for Cats
heading: Personal Magical Powers for Cats
summary: Rules for the Initiative bonus, spell-level cost and Penetration Score of personal powers for cats.
quotes: An Initiative bonus equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude /2).

title: Dragons and Dragon-kind
heading: Dragons and Dragon-kind
summary: Distinguishes serpents, drakes, worms and true dragons, and advises that the largest dragons exceed what the rules can represent and need innovative plans to defeat.

title: Dragons as Characters
heading: Dragons as Characters
summary: Weak dragons can be built with the magical character rules as grogs, companions or magus-equivalents, while non-player dragons need not be strictly balanced.

title: Dragon Concept
heading: Concept
summary: Base Characteristics, Size, required Virtues and suggested Virtues and Flaws when designing a dragon or dragon-kin.
quotes: Dragons and their kin have base Characteristics of 0, and 7 points to spend on improving Characteristics (like human characters).

title: Dragon Season and Abilities
heading: Season and Abilities
summary: Guidance on which seasons suit serpents and dragons and on giving combat opponents a good Brawl.

title: Dragon Might Score and Qualities
heading: Might Score and Qualities
summary: A table of typical Might ranges for each kind of dragon-kin, plus advice on Qualities for breath, gaze and combat statistics.
quotes: A dragon's combat statistics may be improved through liberal use of the Improved Attack, Improved Defense, Improved Damage, and Improved Soak Qualities.

title: Claw and Fang
heading: Claw and Fang
summary: A table of weapon statistics for dragon claws and teeth, with large versions for dragons bigger than Size +2.
quotes: Dragons larger than Size +2 usually have large claws and/or large teeth.

title: Constriction Attacks (Option)
heading: Option: Constriction Attacks
requires: Being type: Dragon, worm or large serpent
summary: An optional rule for dragons and serpents to constrict smaller victims using the grappling rules, depriving them of air.
quotes: A dragon can only constrict a victim whose Size is less than its own.
a constriction attack has the following weapon statistics: Init 0, Atk +3, Dfn 0, Dam n/a
The victim must make a Stamina check every 30 seconds, that is, every five rounds, or suffer the normal effects of deprivation.

title: Transformed Animals
heading: Transformed Animals
summary: Distinguishes Transformed Animals, which are Warped by magic and gain no Magic Might, from Beasts of Virtue.

title: Warping of Animals
heading: Warping
summary: Animals gain Warping points like people and acquire Flaws and then a Virtue at set Warping Scores.
quotes: Once an animal gains a Warping score of 1 it acquires a Minor Flaw, and it gains another Minor Flaw when its Warping score reaches 3.

title: Warped Livestock (Covenant Hook)
heading: Minor Covenant Hook: Warped Livestock
summary: A covenant with Warped animals may farm them for Muto vis, represented by a vis source Boon.

title: Intentionally Warping an Animal
heading: Intentionally Warping an Animal
summary: A cage of change is an enchanted device that gives a captive animal Warping points to make it monstrous for harvesting Muto vis.
quotes: the cage gives the captive in the cage 5 Warping Points

title: Virtues and Flaws from Warping
heading: Virtues and Flaws from Warping
summary: Lists the Supernatural Virtues and Flaws a magically Warped animal may gain, culminating in a Lesser Power at Warping Score 5.
quotes: eventually acquiring a Lesser Power when it reaches a Warping Score of 5

title: Training Creatures
heading: Training Creatures
summary: Any magical beast with Cunning may be tamed over seasons by a magus, magical character or mundane trainer, then trained in tricks.

title: Taming Animals
heading: Taming Animals
summary: Taming is a seasonal activity accumulating points over consecutive seasons until they exceed the creature's Might.
quotes: Taming is complete when the accumulated total of points exceeds the Might of the creature.
**Required Points to Tame a Creature: Might of the Creature**

title: Taming Mundane Beasts
heading: Taming Mundane Beasts
summary: Gives mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and notes that Gift penalties apply because taming is social.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 times Confidence Score

title: Hermetic Trainer
heading: A Hermetic Trainer
summary: A magus tames a creature as a laboratory activity, accumulating points from his Rego (Form) Lab Total less the creature's Might and producing a Lab Text.
quotes: **Taming Points Accumulated Each Season by an Hermetic Tamer: Re(Fo) Lab Total – Creature's Might**

title: Magical Trainer
heading: A Magical Trainer
summary: A character with Master of (Form) Creatures tames creatures of that Form using his Might and Animal Handling less the creature's Might.
quotes: **Taming Points Accumulated Each Season by a Master of Creatures: Trainer's Might + Trainer's Animal Handling – Creature's Might**

title: Mundane Trainer
heading: A Mundane Trainer
summary: A mundane trainer accumulates taming points from Intelligence and Animal Handling less the creature's Might, so can only tame weakly magical beasts.
quotes: **Taming Points Accumulated Each Season by a Mundane Trainer: Int + Animal Handling – Creature's Might**

title: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
heading: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
summary: A tamed animal can be commanded by characters with Intelligence and Animal Handling or to whom it is loyal, and is not under a continuing mystical effect.

title: Animal Loyalty
heading: Loyalty
summary: A tamed creature gains a Loyal Personality Trait toward its tamer, which can be raised or transferred with extra seasons and tested with a Loyalty Test.
quotes: **Loyalty Test: Loyal Personality Trait + stress die vs Ease Factor**
Each additional season of training increases the Loyal trait by +1, to a maximum of +3.

title: Training Animal Abilities
heading: Training Abilities
summary: Characters with Animal Handling can train a tamed animal's Abilities with the standard training rules, with a Loyalty test for new Abilities.
quotes: make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

title: Animal Ken and Taming
heading: Animal Ken
summary: Describes how Animal Ken lets a character reason with animals, add to taming totals and give more complex commands.

title: Trained Groups of Animals
heading: Trained Groups
summary: A character can lead tamed animals in combat as a trained group, using Animal Handling instead of Leadership to set group size.

title: Commanding a Creature
heading: Commanding a Creature
summary: Commanding a tamed creature is a Presence plus Animal Handling roll against an Ease Factor set by how familiar, stressful or frightening the task is.
quotes: **Command Beast: Presence + Animal Handling (or Ride or Magic Lore) + stress die vs Ease Factor**

title: Designing Giants
heading: Designing Giants
summary: Humanoid beings larger than human size get their Size from the Gigantic Quality.

title: How Big is a Giant?
heading: How Big is a Giant?
summary: A table of approximate height and weight for each Size, noting that Size determines height and weight rather than the reverse.
quotes: a character's height and weight are determined by his Size Characteristic, not the other way round

title: Giant Concept
heading: Concept
summary: Story roles and suggested Virtues and Flaws for giants, which use the Magic Human rules with the Gigantic Quality applied after Characteristics.
quotes: Giants should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4.

title: Giant Season and Abilities
heading: Season and Abilities
summary: Spring giants suffer child-like Characteristic penalties and language Abilities must be bought with the giant's season experience.

title: Giant Might and Qualities
heading: Might and Qualities
summary: All giants take the Major Quality Gigantic, repeated for larger Sizes, which drives the Might needed.
quotes: All giants must take the Major Quality, Gigantic; giants larger than Size +2 should take it more than once.

title: Giant Finishing Touches
heading: Finishing Touches
summary: Giants use clubs, with combat statistics computed normally allowing for the Gigantic Quality's effects.

title: Giants in Combat
heading: Giants in Combat
summary: An optional rule of thumb giving giants a defensive bonus against scuffling, grappling and disarming by smaller opponents, and notes on Corpus spells against giants.
quotes: a giant gains a special defensive bonus equal to double the difference between its Size and a smaller opponent's

title: Norse Giants and Trolls
heading: Norse Giants and Trolls
requires: Being type: Norse giant or troll
summary: Options for building Norse giants and trolls, including elemental Form affiliations, typical powers and a size-changing rule.
quotes: When the giant reduces its size, its Strength diminishes by 2 and its Quickness improves by 1 for each point of Size reduction.

title: Non-Human Giants
heading: Non-Human Giants
summary: To build oversized elementals, spirits or animals, use the rules for that creature type and add the Gigantic Quality.
quotes: simply choose Gigantic as one of the creature's Qualities

title: Spirit Votary (Virtue and Character Type)
heading: New Virtue: Spirit Votary
summary: A Free Supernatural Virtue making the character a Mythic Companion who must take Spiritual Pact plus further supernatural Virtues and the Pagan Flaw.
quotes: A Spirit Votary is required to take the Spiritual Pact Virtue (see below), along with either three Minor Supernatural Virtues or one Major Supernatural Virtue.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.103 Blood of Heroes

title: Spiritual Pact
heading: New Virtue: Spiritual Pact
summary: A character with a pact to a Magical spirit spends a Confidence Point and rolls to draw a Might Pool from the spirit, which then powers the spirit's abilities until exhausted.
quotes: Make a Presence + Magic Lore + stress die roll: this is the amount of Magic Might Pool that the character acquires from his spiritual master.

title: Magic Kin
heading: Magic Kin
summary: Introduces magic kin lineages that can be used as templates for magic characters, each with Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws to take at character creation.
quotes: that characters designed to belong to that family should strongly consider taking during character creation

title: Atlanteans
heading: Atlanteans
summary: Template for ocean-dwelling Atlantean characters with water-based Inherited Virtues, an exile Flaw and powers working over water-ways.
quotes: Other water creatures will only obey a summons if a Presence + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor of 6 + Creature Size is successfully made.

title: Flame Dancers
heading: Flame Dancers
summary: Template for people possessed by the power of fire, with fire-related powers and compulsions.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Greater Power: *Let the Bonfire Burn*, Personal Power: *Endurance of the Flame Dancer*

title: Forgotten Gods
heading: Forgotten Gods
summary: Template for old gods who survive in living form, built around a Focus or Greater Power describing their sphere of influence.
quotes: As characters, they should take a Greater Power or Focus Power that describes this influence.

title: Loamwalkers
heading: Loamwalkers
summary: Template for tree-spirits living in human shape, with powers to travel between trees and change between tree and human form.
quotes: **Common Flaws:** Dark Secret (Loamwalker), Essential Flaw (minor): Antisocial (Presence), Fear (fire), Baneful Circumstances (must be rooted into the earth)

title: Lost Children
heading: Lost Children
summary: Template for abandoned children who became ageless Magical beings, designed with a child's Size and Characteristic penalties.
quotes: so to play one you should design a character with the Size and Characteristics penalties of a child

title: Men of the Lake
heading: Men of the Lake
requires: Magic kin: Man of the Lake
summary: Template for sentient lake beings with water powers, a seasonal society and a network of lake regiones.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Greater Power: *Drown* (see page 137), Personal Power: *Simulacrum Form*, Ritual Power: *Command the Waters*, Focus Power: *Memory of Water*, (Lake) Regio Network.

title: Orphan Born
heading: Orphan Born
summary: Template for humans conceived beyond the veil of the spirit world, who can become incorporeal and see spirits.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Greater Power: *Incorporeal Form*, Personal Power: *Ghostly/Physical Form*, Second Sight

title: People of the Clouds
heading: People of the Clouds
requires: Magic kin: Person of the Clouds
summary: Template for sky-sailors who command the wind and can fly or sail ships through the air.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Greater Power: *Sail the Wind*

title: The Stoneskinned
heading: The Stoneskinned
summary: Template for people of living rock whose stone powers scale with age or Might and who turn to stone in daylight.
quotes: These stats are Init +X, Atk +2X, Dfn +X, Dam +2X, where X is either the character's (Might Score / 5) or his (age / 10).

title: Warders of Mystery
heading: Warders of Mystery
summary: Template for the society of Auditores who keep magic secret, with a power to perceive distant places through Arcane Connections.
quotes: **Inherited Virtues:** Greater Power: *Perceive the Distant Truths*

title: Drowned Men
heading: Drowned Men
summary: Drowned Men are sailors who passed through a magical regio and returned as creatures of Magic.

title: Drowned Men Characters
heading: Drowned Men Characters
summary: Drowned Men must take the Transformed (Being) Virtue and commonly have a sea Flaw, Greater Immunity (drowning) and the Servant of the Ocean Flaw.

title: Planning for Drowning
heading: Planning for Drowning
summary: A character can try to become a Drowned Man by contacting and bargaining with a powerful water entity before surrendering to the water, using two rolls.
quotes: **Determine Contact Method: Int + Magic Lore + Stress die vs Ease Factor of 12**
**Negotiation for Power: Int + Bargain + Stress Die vs Ease Factor of 6 + Might / 5**

title: Burned and Buried Men
heading: Burned and Buried Men
summary: A person might be saved from fire or burial by a magical creature of Ignem or Terram and gain Virtues like a Drowned Man.

title: Revenants, the Walking Dead
heading: Revenants, the Walking Dead
summary: Explains revenants as animate corpses driven by a spirit, and that their physical statistics also serve corpses animated by spells.
quotes: The physical statistics of a revenant are also usable for corpses that have been animated by spells such as *The Walking Corpse*

title: Designing Revenants
heading: Designing Revenants
summary: Revenants are usually Spring or Summer Magic Humans with the No Fatigue and Improved Soak Qualities to reflect their resilience.
quotes: They should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4: Magic Characters.

title: Fighting the Walking Dead
heading: Fighting the Walking Dead
summary: Describes how spells and weapons affect revenants, including the rule that they cannot be Incapacitated and the legendary methods that destroy their animating spirit.
quotes: they cannot be Incapacitated; treat Incapacitating wounds as Heavy wounds instead
Learning the method for destroying a revenant may require a story, or if the storyguide prefers she can assign it an Ease Factor of 9 on an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll.

title: Resistance to Piercing Weapons (Option)
heading: Option: Resistance to Piercing Weapons
summary: An optional rule giving revenants extra Soak against piercing weapons, or making such weapons useless.
quotes: The troupe may wish to grant revenants an additional +10 Soak bonus against such weapons, or simply rule them totally ineffective.

title: Animating Corpses with Magic
heading: Animating Corpses with Magic
summary: Corpses animated by Rego Corpus spells or possessing spirits use revenant statistics with limited Qualities, and no Might unless a spirit controls them.
quotes: Its Brawl skill is nominally 3

title: Magi in Final Twilight
heading: Magi in Final Twilight
summary: A magus entering Final Twilight may rarely become a Magical being, with Might set by guideline ranges or formulas tied to an Art or Ability.
quotes: The Might Score of a magus Transformed by Twilight should generally be around 20 to 40.
related: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.24 Great Beasts

title: Spirits as Characters
heading: Spirits as Characters
summary: Spirits are incorporeal, immortal beings that cannot affect or be sensed by matter without powers or magic, communicating through Silent Speech, and take the Magic Spirit Virtue.

title: Spirit Concept
heading: Concept
summary: How to set Characteristics for spirits, that Size is meaningless until a spirit takes physical form, and that all spirits have the Magical Air Flaw.
quotes: For plants and spirits of non-living objects, assume that all Characteristics begin at zero and apply 7 characteristic points in the usual fashion.

title: Taxonomy of the Invisible World
heading: Taxonomy of the Invisible World
summary: Defines the terms spirit, genius, animus, Daimon and Airy Spirit used for the rules in this chapter.

title: Spirit Season and Abilities
heading: Season and Abilities
summary: Which seasons suit different kinds of spirits and why spirits often take Reduced Abilities.

title: Spirit Might and Qualities
heading: Might and Qualities
summary: Spirits need no Quality to be incorporeal or immortal, but need Powers to be seen or to affect the world, so most of their Qualities go to Powers.

title: Powers of the Spirits
heading: Powers of the Spirits
summary: Introduces common spirit powers, which must penetrate Magic Resistance, with Ritual-like powers permanently reducing the spirit's Might.
quotes: Naturally, any power that affects another being must penetrate its Magic Resistance.

title: Spirits as a Source of Vis
heading: Spirits as a Source of Vis
summary: Explains how much raw vis a spirit contains, when it can be distilled after the spirit is slain, and the vis from corporeal bodies and Presence.
quotes: typically 1 pawn of an appropriate Form per magnitude of their Might

title: Spirit Power: Control Human
heading: Control Human
summary: A spirit power to direct a human, who may resist with an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor set by the spirit's Might.
quotes: To break free, the target makes an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor equal to 9 + magnitude of spirit's Might.

title: Spirit Power: Donning the Corporeal Veil
heading: Donning the Corporeal Veil
summary: A spirit power to create and animate a physical body that shares the spirit's statistics but is limited in Size.
quotes: The body created with this power has the same physical statistics as the spirit, but can have a maximum Size of +1.

title: Spirit Power: Eidolon
heading: Eidolon
summary: A spirit power creating an illusory form visible and audible to material beings.
quotes: Creates an illusionary form that is visible and audible to material beings.

title: Spirit Power: Ghost Touch
heading: Ghost Touch
summary: A spirit power to move or hurl objects, with weight limit and damage determined by the Might points spent.
quotes: For 1 Might point, a maximum of 5 pounds can be moved; every additional Might point doubles this weight limit.

title: Spirit Power: Manifestation
heading: Manifestation
summary: A spirit power to take control of plants or animals by touch, with the amount controlled set by the Might points spent.
quotes: For an extra 2 Might points, a group of ten standard creatures or plants (or the equivalent mass) can be controlled.

title: Spirit Power: Material Anchor
heading: Material Anchor
summary: A ritual-like spirit power forming an Arcane Connection to a person or place, or making an object a connection to the spirit, with cost set by duration.
quotes: If the connection is to last for hours or days, then it costs just 1 point; a connection that lasts for weeks or months costs 2 points; years or decades costs 3 points; and indefinite Arcane Connections cost 4 points.

title: Spirit Power: Presence
heading: Presence
summary: A spirit power giving awareness of a domain whose size depends on its Might, doubling Might for Tether Strength and yielding yearly vis.
quotes: The area controlled by the spirit can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of vis of an appropriate Form

title: Spirit Power: Regio
heading: Regio
summary: A ritual-like power for a spirit with Presence to form a Magic regio with one or more layers of rising aura strength.
quotes: each additional layer has an aura 2 points stronger than the previous layer, up to a maximum of 10

title: Spirit Power: Stasis
heading: Stasis
summary: A ritual-like power making a Magic-aura area timeless, so residents' aging points become Warping points and long-term residents cannot leave the aura.
quotes: However, any aging points are applied to the character as Warping points instead.

title: Daimons
heading: Daimons
summary: Daimons, the Named Spirits, remain in the Magic Realm and act on Earth only through short-lived Aspects with their own Might, which are constant Arcane Connections to the parent.
quotes: A Daimon is a permanent resident of the Magic Realm and cannot enter the material world; instead, it creates an Aspect as its agent on Earth.
